description: Transcribed published DynaHug metrics for the ReGenBench baseline reference-comparison dataset. Numbers are transcribed verbatim from the cited paper; they are NOT re-derived in this repository. See docs/reference-dynahug-metrics.md and docs/comparison-methodology.md.

source.title: Malicious ML Model Detection by Learning Dynamic Behaviors
source.tables: Table 5 (per-cluster), Table 6 (vs SOTA), Table 7 (analysis-type ablation), Table 8 (feature-set ablation)

model_context.training: 2,000 benign PTMs (text-generation cluster), supervised only on benign, presence+frequency syscall features
model_context.dataset_split: 80:10:10 train/validation/test; malicious in val/test = half MalHug + half MalHug-injected
model_context.observability: strace -c count pass during torch.load(weights_only=False) deserialization in Docker

table_5_per_cluster.caption: DynaHug's performance on three (3) task-based clusters.
table_5_per_cluster.meta: Benign Real = benign HF PTMs; Malicious Real = HF-flagged/known malicious; Injected = MalHug-injected payloads. Numbers are raw counts and ratios reported in the paper.

table_6_vs_sota.caption: Comparison of DynaHug vs. open-source SOTA's performance.
table_6_vs_sota.malicious_total_note: Malicious (2025) = 25 Real + 1000 MalHug + 1000 PyPI-injected on the text-generation test set.

table_7_analysis_ablation.caption: DynaHug's performance under different analysis types.
table_7_analysis_ablation.note: Dynamic is ~2x more effective than static (precision 0.9995 vs 0.5); hybrid equals dynamic.

table_8_feature_ablation.caption: DynaHug's effectiveness with varying feature sets ('freq'=frequency, 'seq'=sequence, 'proc'=process).

feature_sets.presence_freq_seq_procseq: presence + frequency + syscall sequence + process sequence

table_8_feature_ablation.note: Frequency improves recall+F1 over presence only by ~19% (recall 0.8326->0.9931) and ~10% (F1 0.9086->0.9963). Adding sequence/proc-seq reduces precision and F1.

claims: DynaHug achieves up to 0.9963 F1 (text-generation cluster).
DynaHug is up to 44% more effective than the best static baselines (PickleScan/ModelScan, F1 0.6902 vs 0.9963).
DynaHug outperforms closest competitor GPT-5.2 by ~5% (0.9963 vs 0.9393 F1).
DynaHug is 33% more effective than Llama-3.1 (0.9963 vs 0.7483 F1).
Dynamic analysis is ~2x static (precision 0.9995 vs 0.5, Table 7).
